items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Now my brother and I had always played violin and I had played a little bit of the peck horn, and he played E-flat alto horn, in my father's band at picnics and things.

ctx.x: But you were talking about the influences though in this particular mixed neighborhood.

Ah, here's what happened. Now my brother and I had always played violin and I had played a little bit of the peck horn, and he played E-flat alto horn, in my father's band at picnics and things. It was a regular band you know, marching band style, that kind of stuff. And so forth.

And so I had musical training already. Now one night, it was a mixed neighborhood as I say, on Lake and Polina Lincoln Street on the West Side of Chicago. And there were eight colored men, blind colored men who heard this music across the street. Two or three basses and banjos and a guitar, mandolin and guitar. And they were singing spirituals. Gospel music. And my brother and I were, let me preface this by saying this. We were tough little monkeys in those days. Rough kids, you know, that's a tough neighborhood.…
